 AIRF presented its demands to the 8th CPC, seeking better pay scales and risk, hardship, hazardous-duty and dress allowances for its employees. It highlighted railway work’s round-the-clock and raised concerns for running staff, track maintainers, technicians.
 Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 2 Nov 2026, 07:38 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Share via Advertisement At the 8th CPC meeting in Mumbai, AIRF presented demands seeking better pay scales and risk, hardship, hazardous-duty and dress allowances for Railway employees. (AI generated image for representational purposes only) AI Quick Read The All India Railwaymen’s Federation (AIRF) has in a letter to the 8th pay commission, after their meeting with the panel during the Mumbai visit, reiterated demands made for Railway employees.
 The letter briefed the areas of discussion during the meeting, noting that they have sought higher pay scales and risk allowances, with crucial demands for loco and traffic running staff.
 Advertisement 8th CPC meeting: What was discussed?
 The meeting began with discussions on the general issues such as minimum wage and Railway-specific allowances , while the second part focused on issues related to loco and traffic running staff, the third raised concerns for track maintainers and allied category of P. Way staff, and lastly on issues of technicians across Railway departments, it said.
 Also Read | Florida jet crash: 9 dead as Learjet slams into roadside, erupting in fireball “It was emphasized that the Indian Railways is unique, which cannot be compared to any other department of Union Government, because Railways operate round-the-clock, 24X7, throughout the year, in all weathers and climatic conditions, at different parts of the country having distinct geographical and environmental conditions,” the letter stated.
 The federation added that the Railways are considered to be the “Second Line of Defence” after the Army because of the fact that, during Natural Calamities, war-like situation and Pandemic, it is the Railwaymen and the Indian Railways that serve the Nation on the forefront.
 Advertisement AIRF's full list of demands
 Higher pay scales: It said that working conditions and other service-related issues of the Railwaymen, particularly in the wake of fast pace of modernization, means they deserve placing in higher pay-scales as skilled workers who either maintain or operate different assets, i.e. rolling stock, signaling and track etc.
 Also Read | Festive demand sends mixed signals as shoppers turn cautious Special Allowances: It also explained that, keeping in view the number of casualties and grievous injuries sustained during the course of employment, Railwaymen across categories should be considered for “Special Allowances” — i.e. Risk & Hardship Allowance , Hazardous Duty Allowance, Hill Allowance and Dress Allowance.
 Treat track maintainers at par with the Technicians of other Engineering Disciplines of the Indian Railways as due to drastic improvement in track geometry and precision, they are required to possess better know-how and technical knowledge.
 Advertisement Also Read | Flying abroad? How Digi Yatra could make airport entry and boarding easier? Demanded “Certain Specific Allowances” for track maintainers, patrolman, keyman and gateman of the Civil Engineering Department.
 For technicians of all engineering disciplines of the Railways it was demanded that, they should be fairly treated and placed in better pay-scales, besides merger of certain intermediate pay-scales into one, to facilitate better promotional prospects.
 Due to hardship and risk involved in performance of duties, AIRF also demanded adequate Risk & Hardship Allowance and Dress Allowance for all technicians.
